## Read first

Read `AGENTS.md`, [scope](scope.qmd), [architecture](architecture.qmd), and
the relevant operation or subsystem record. Use the active Project Control
task for live status and ownership. Closed Todo files and archived plans record
earlier intent; they do not define current package capability.

## Architectural orientation for contributors

Biological machine learning is the organizing principle: make representations,
relationships, architectures, and objectives for cellular systems natural to
construct, train, and execute. Read the [learning-problem architecture](architecture.qmd#organizing-the-learning-problem)
before extending model-facing APIs. Evaluate the representation and objective
alongside numerical execution, rather than treating learning as an adapter to
a universal cell-transition runtime.

`Cell`, persistent state, trajectories, and population mechanics are optional
capabilities. Dense attention, static representation learners, transformers,
recurrent models, conditional computation, and hybrids remain equally valid.
An operation can exploit biological structure without requiring every model to
use it. Keep the framework's general neural-network expressiveness intact.

For interpretation claims, use the [question-relative identifiability boundary](architecture.qmd#scientific-questions-and-identifiability).
Explicit structure can clarify a learning problem; inference depends on its
model family, assumptions, and observations or interventions. Neither biological
naming nor latent-state ambiguity settles identifiability on its own. GlassHelix
investigates the formal inferability question; Cellerator supplies reusable
architectures and learning mechanisms.

This is architectural guidance, not a request to rewrite current APIs or proof
that every intended capability is implemented. The
[modeling and neural-network backbone](architecture.qmd#modeling-and-neural-network-backbone)
records the six conceptual concerns and distinguishes existing foundations from
remaining capabilities. Use the source routing and implementation evidence
below for the bounded change actually authorized.

## Implementation references

The [implementation style guide](development/implementation_style.md) describes maintained contributor conventions. The [operation registry](development/operation_registry.md) is a historical inventory; confirm any entry against current source and the routing map.

The language compiler and its build/API documentation are maintained in
[Texo](https://github.com/tumlinso/Texo). The [source routing guide](development/routing.md)
and its generated map are the path-level inventory: they list current role,
owner, target, disposition, maturity, consumers, and evidence. This page
summarizes build routes and points to that map; it is not a duplicate source
catalog.

## Mandatory native toolchain and installed dependencies

Every root CMake build requires CMake 3.28 or newer, Ninja 1.11 or newer,
Clang 18 or newer, and the matching `clang-scan-deps` executable. Set
`CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER_CLANG_SCAN_DEPS` to that scanner when autodetection is not
appropriate. Cellerator C++ and CUDA targets require at least C++20. Its named
modules are built and exported by the normal package build. The core module is
always exported as
`Cellerator::core_module`; request it with
`find_package(Cellerator CONFIG REQUIRED COMPONENTS core_module)` and import it
as `cellerator.core;`. When NN is enabled, use the `nn_modules` package
component and target `Cellerator::nn_modules` for `import cellerator.nn;`.
Module consumers must set `CMAKE_CXX_EXTENSIONS OFF` before creating importer
targets, so Clang builds them in strict C++20 or C++23 mode rather than
`gnu++20`. CUDA translation units keep using public headers and do not import
named modules.

Native builds require the separately installed HDF5-only
[AnnData++](https://github.com/tumlinso/anndatapp) package version 1.0 or newer;
the example below uses `v1.0.0`.
The package must be built with HDF5 on and Zarr off. This is Cellerator's sole
native H5AD path: the old reader is retired, with no legacy parser or fallback.
See its [declared encoding boundary](https://github.com/tumlinso/anndatapp/blob/v1.0.0/docs/h5ad.md)
and [native dependency installation guide](https://github.com/tumlinso/anndatapp/blob/v1.0.0/docs/storage-dependencies.md).
The native H5AD route accepts the supported modern subset, including sparse
CSR/CSC. Root CMake requires `anndatapp::anndatapp` to be discoverable; it does not
download or silently replace that dependency.

Normal builds also require installed Velocity++ 0.1.1 or newer by default.
Expose its prefix alongside AnnData++ through `CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH`; Cellerator
uses `find_package(velocitypp CONFIG REQUIRED)` without a bundled fallback.
`CELLERATOR_ENABLE_VELOCITY=OFF` skips this dependency and the FP16 extension.
The installed `velocity` component exports `Cellerator::velocity` and
`import cellerator.velocity;`, re-exporting Velocity++ with Cellerator-owned
binary16 operations under `cellerator::velocity`. Its caller-storage API and
FP16 boundary are described in [the adapter guide](../src/ops/velocity/README.md).
The old allocating `velocity` module is retired from the active build; the
former local checkout is preserved for recovery and is not compiled.

Build and install that dependency at the pinned revision, then configure the
Cellerator package against its prefix:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/tumlinso/anndatapp.git /tmp/anndatapp
git -C /tmp/anndatapp checkout --detach v1.0.0
cmake -S /tmp/anndatapp -B /tmp/anndatapp-build -G Ninja \
  -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=clang++-18 \
  -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER_CLANG_SCAN_DEPS=clang-scan-deps-18 \
  -DANNDATAPP_ENABLE_HDF5=ON \
  -DANNDATAPP_ENABLE_ZARR=OFF \
  -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=/tmp/anndatapp-install
cmake --build /tmp/anndatapp-build
cmake --install /tmp/anndatapp-build

# Build/install Velocity++ >=0.1.1 separately against this AnnData++ prefix.
# Set VELOCITYPP_PREFIX to that installation, or disable velocity explicitly.

cmake -S . -B build-cpu -G Ninja \
  -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=clang++-18 \
  -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER_CLANG_SCAN_DEPS=clang-scan-deps-18 \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="/tmp/anndatapp-install;${VELOCITYPP_PREFIX}" \
  -DCELLERATOR_ENABLE_CUDA=OFF
cmake --build build-cpu
```

An installed C++ consumer links the module targets directly:

```cmake
set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 20)
set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)
set(CMAKE_CXX_EXTENSIONS OFF)
find_package(Cellerator CONFIG REQUIRED COMPONENTS core_module)
find_package(anndatapp CONFIG REQUIRED)
target_link_libraries(my_model PRIVATE Cellerator::core_module anndatapp::anndatapp)
```

The corresponding C++ translation unit imports both interfaces:

```cpp
import cellerator.core;
import anndatapp.h5ad;
```

For the optional native NN module, configure Cellerator with NN enabled and use
`find_package(Cellerator CONFIG REQUIRED COMPONENTS nn_modules)` with
`Cellerator::nn_modules`. Keep `CMAKE_CXX_EXTENSIONS OFF` for its importer as
well. The installed module sources are compiled by the consumer's
module-capable build; module support is not an optional side build.

## Current high-level routes

```text
include/Cellerator/   public native contracts, including cell.hh and cells/
src/                  native implementation (several owners and generations)
bindings/python/      optional pybind Python extension
bindings/torch/       optional compiled Torch adapters
python/cellerator/    installed Python package and Torch modules
tests/                native, Python, and subsystem checks
examples/biology/      host-only typed biological relation examples
examples/native_cell/  host-only native Cell capability examples
bench/, experiments/  measured candidates and source-bound experiments
docs/                 architecture, capability boundaries, and evidence links
```

The [biological relation example](https://github.com/tumlinso/Cellerator/blob/main/examples/biology/README.md) exercises public typed-relation and execution-lifetime contracts on the host; it does not execute a numerical kernel or load a dataset.

## Native Cell examples

The [native data guide](native_data.qmd) covers canonical dependency patterns,
specialist tensor owners/views, layout maps and prepared multi-device bindings
below cells and models. Host consumers link `Cellerator::native_data`; the
smaller `Cellerator::tensor` surface and optional `Cellerator::native_data_cuda`
keep numerical format and CUDA dependencies explicit. The focused
`CELLERATOR_BUILD_NATIVE_DATA_TESTS=ON` route builds focused native-data tests
without enabling the full root test suite (`CELLERATOR_BUILD_TESTS=OFF`).

The [`event_forward.cc`](../examples/native_cell/event_forward.cc),
[`multimodal.cc`](../examples/native_cell/multimodal.cc), and
[`foundation.cc`](../examples/native_cell/foundation.cc) examples use the
Torch-free typed Cell and adapter headers. The package baseline is C++20;
dense-expression selection uses C++20 `std::span`. The optional `CellViews` runtime bridge links
`Cellerator::libCellerator` for its out-of-line destructor; the typed binding
needs neither that symbol nor RTTI. Configure a host-only tree with Python, Torch, CUDA, NN,
tokenization, and sparse support disabled, then build and run the examples:

```sh
cmake -S . -B build/cell-host -G Ninja \
  -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=clang++-18 \
  -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER_CLANG_SCAN_DEPS=clang-scan-deps-18 \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=/path/to/anndatapp-install \
  -DCELLERATOR_ENABLE_CUDA=OFF \
  -DCELLERATOR_ENABLE_PYTHON=OFF \
  -DCELLERATOR_ENABLE_TORCH=OFF \
  -DCELLERATOR_ENABLE_NN=OFF \
  -DCELLERATOR_ENABLE_NN_CUDA=OFF \
  -DCELLERATOR_ENABLE_TOKENIZATION=OFF \
  -DCELLERATOR_ENABLE_SPARSE_SUPPORT=OFF \
  -DCELLERATOR_ENABLE_MODELING=OFF \
  -DCELLERATOR_ENABLE_CONDITIONAL=OFF \
  -DCELLERATOR_ENABLE_HARDWARE_PROBE=OFF \
  -DCELLERATOR_ENABLE_CELLSHARD=OFF \
  -DCELLERATOR_BUILD_TORCH_EXAMPLES=OFF \
  -DCELLERATOR_BUILD_TESTS=ON
cmake --build build/cell-host \
  --target cellerator_cell_core_test cellerator_cell_views_bridge_test \
    cellerator_typed_core_no_rtti_test cellerator_cell_adapters_test \
    cellerator_cell_event_forward_example cellerator_cell_multimodal_example \
    cellerator_cell_foundation_example
ctest --test-dir build/cell-host -R cell_ --output-on-failure
```

The event example uses a deterministic evaluator and storage-owned append to
extend the continuing instance while copied prefix selections retain prior
boundaries. It rejects stale or foreign continuations and is not a trained
Karyoplast model. The multimodal example demonstrates event, expression,
identity, and custom access with explicit edits and an optional runtime bridge.
The foundation example explores shared portions, joint operations, pooled
batching, host-buffer movement and caller-supplied execution costs, cache
validity, and retained asynchronous resources. These are host contracts, not a
distributed scheduler or a performance measurement. Device-placement checks
propagate metadata without executing on a GPU.

Newer native organization includes `src/common`, `src/structure`, `src/support`,
`src/indexing`, `src/gating`, `src/layout`, and `src/ops`. The public header
paths are mixed-generation: structure uses `include/Cellerator/structure`,
support/indexing/gating use `include/Cellerator/compute/{support,indexing,gating}`,
physical projections use `include/Cellerator/compute/projection`, and newer
operation families use `include/Cellerator/ops`. Existing `compute`, `math`,
`execution`, `runtime`, and compatibility paths still own real code and
consumers; Cellerator's language compiler is maintained in Texo. Numerical
geometry planning and execution preparation remain Cellerator responsibilities.
Do not infer that all files have been consolidated from the presence of a newer
directory.
CellPack headers live under `include/Cellerator/geometry`; the former
`include/CellPack` forwarding directory has been removed. Include
`Cellerator/geometry/...` directly. The `cellpack` namespace and `CellPack::`
targets retain their existing contracts. Use the exhaustive
[routing map](development/routing.md) before moving or archiving a path.

The independent SpMM numerical reference is installed as
`Cellerator::spmm_reference`, with headers under `Cellerator/math/reference`.
Borrowed CSR/native-tile adaptation and BELL lowering belong to
`Cellerator::physical_projection`; CUDA operand packing remains the optional
`Cellerator::packed_dense_operand` target. Their headers are under
`Cellerator/layout/projection`, with the existing native-tile adapter header at
`Cellerator/compute/projection/native_tile_view.hh`. Include these canonical headers directly. The historical execution-plan
header and old `compute/math` forwarding paths have been retired. See the [compatibility archive](history/compat/README.md)
for exact original sources and provenance.

After installing the host package, verify these headers and libraries with:

```sh
cmake -S tests/package/reference_consumer -B /tmp/cellerator-reference-consumer \
  -G Ninja -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=clang++-18 \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=/path/to/cellerator-install
cmake --build /tmp/cellerator-reference-consumer
ctest --test-dir /tmp/cellerator-reference-consumer --output-on-failure
```

For a focused staging install, `CELLERATOR_REFERENCE_EXPORTS` may point directly
to the installed directory containing `CelleratorReferenceTargets.cmake` and
`CelleratorProjectionTargets.cmake`. This validates the two installed owners
without requiring unrelated SDK libraries to be built.

## Configure and build

Use the mandatory Clang/Ninja and installed HDF5-only AnnData++ baseline
from the section above. For a Python host-only extension with Product2:

```sh
cmake -S . -B build-cpu -G Ninja \
  -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=clang++-18 \
  -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER_CLANG_SCAN_DEPS=clang-scan-deps-18 \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=/path/to/anndatapp-install \
  -DCELLERATOR_ENABLE_CUDA=OFF \
  -DCELLERATOR_ENABLE_PYTHON=ON \
  -DCELLERATOR_ENABLE_TORCH=OFF
cmake --build build-cpu --target cellerator_python_extensions
```

The Python distribution's default build is host-oriented: Python is enabled,
CUDA and compiled Torch adapters are disabled, and Product2 follows the Python
option. `CELLERATOR_ENABLE_CUDA` accepts `AUTO`, `ON`, or `OFF`;
`CELLERATOR_ENABLE_TORCH` requires the CUDA indexed-mechanism owner and a
compatible Torch/CUDA build. `CELLERATOR_ENABLE_TOKENIZATION` is a separate
optional ATen facility. Native C++ consumers keep Python/Torch options off by
default. See [Python bindings](development/python-bindings.md) for install and
import behavior.

Inspect the configured build rather than relying on old target lists:

```sh
cmake --build build-cpu --target help
ctest --test-dir build-cpu --output-on-failure
```

Tests may also be focused executables and not all are registered with CTest.
Use the target and command associated with the changed contract. For CUDA
memory or synchronization changes, run the appropriate Compute Sanitizer tool
on a focused binary. Report checks that were unavailable or not run.

## Numerical and performance evidence

Follow the [numerical policy](architecture.qmd#numerical-policy) and the
[performance and validation guide](performance_validation.qmd). Source-level
defaults and an architectural default are not interchangeable. For a
configured build, inspect storage, arithmetic, accumulation, and output types
along with each operation's supported combinations.

Benchmark complete relevant costs, including preparation, transfer,
conversion, allocation, routing, synchronization, execution, and output mapping
when they apply. Use the repository benchmark mutex and avoid overlapping
measurements. A kernel result is not a complete-operation claim; a synthetic
fixture is not biological validation. Preserve source-bound reports and
negative results unchanged.

## Documentation and review

Render the book after prose changes:

```sh
quarto render docs --to html
```

For a code change, validate the relevant build, source tests, package import,
and consumer paths. Check links and current-versus-proposed status. Do not run a
GPU benchmark as part of documentation generation.

Before changing a contract, answer: which identities and orders enter and
leave; what is immutable; how do values and structure invalidate preparation;
what is the physical mapping; who owns memory, streams and parameters; which
callers and tests exercise it; what is the complete supported backend; and
what evidence supports correctness, scientific validity, and performance
separately?

Public native callers should include `<Cellerator/...>` headers. Do not add
public headers that reach into `src/`. Preserve real sibling and native
consumers when moving implementations, and retain unique entry points until
they have a reviewed replacement.
